title: Blender's chimpanzee, and the first fetched subject in this corpus with a thousand-triangle silhouette

criterion.says: Blender's test model of the chimpanzee Suzanne.

acceptanceClass.because: A closed organic body under the framing rule's general position. Nothing here is analytic: the silhouette turns continuously and every boundary pixel has its own sub-pixel offset, which is what makes a coverage comparison over the whole boundary the instrument rather than any one edge.

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

subjects.name: Suzanne
subjects.notes: POSITION, NORMAL, TANGENT and TEXCOORD_0 over a closed subdivision cage. The textures the file carries are NOT read by this case -- the material below declares its own colour -- so what is compared is the geometry and the single material's binding to it.

source.pinReason: the corpus-wide pin every manifest in this tree already cites

camera.derivation: The framing rule of src/gltf/Framing.h, quoted so the runner can refuse a mismatch rather than trust it. World bounds [-1.336914, -0.974609, -0.800781] to [1.336914, 0.950195, 0.825684], so centre = [0.0, -0.012206999999999968, 0.012451500000000004] and radius = 1.8370911115282904 m. yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from a 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL. distance = radius / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 = 13.119851665490499, and the eye is centre + (cos20*cos35, sin20, cos20*sin35) * distance. clipStart is distance - radius and clipEnd is distance + radius. QUOTED FROM THE RULE'S OWN OUTPUT, not recomputed beside it: the bounds are the AABB of the TRANSFORMED VERTICES, and an authoring helper that transformed the eight corners of the local AABB produced a looser box wherever a node rotates -- 1.536e-07 m of eye, five orders past the runner's tolerance.
camera.note: THE ENGINE'S OWN ANSWER, QUOTED (board:1398). Every number here is read from the framing rule's output for this subject -- eye, aim, yfov and both clip planes -- rather than recomputed by the authoring helper, which bounded each primitive by the eight transformed corners of its local AABB and therefore always at least as loosely as the engine bounds the transformed vertices. A looser radius moves the eye back, and 93 cases declared a camera the rule does not derive. `ADerivedCameraIsTheFramingRuleAndNotAQuotation` recomputes all of it and refuses a mismatch, so what this declaration does is PIN the viewpoint, never choose it.

light.note: The material below emits, so nothing has to arrive for the picture to exist. A light here would add a lobe neither side is being asked about.

world.note: Declared and zero rather than left factory, so the picture is a function of this manifest and not of a Blender default. At zero bounces an emission shader returns its emission alone, so this changes no covered pixel -- it removes the background from the DECLARATION rather than from the render.

material.note: Emission, one colour per glTF material, keyed by the name the FILE gives it. One material and one mesh, so this states that the binding reached the body.

default.note: The binary mask and the emitted colour in one render. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it. A still costs one frame, so the full 1280x720 is affordable here where an animated case has to buy its grid.

seed-shift.note: The same recipe with the sampler's seed moved. At one sample per pixel of a deterministic emission there is nothing for a seed to change, so any pixel that moves between these two renders is the oracle's own noise rather than a disagreement with us -- which is what makes this the instrument floor instead of an assumption about it.

notes: A coverage case. The model's own textures and its metallic-roughness row are not what this decides, and saying so is what keeps the criterion honest.

subjectFrameFraction.note: The fraction of the frame the subject's projected area covers at frame 0, RE-HARVESTED after the camera became the framing rule's own answer (board:1398). Recomputed by the runner on every run and refused on mismatch, so this line PINS the framing and never chooses it; seeded from that recomputation, it is a drift detector rather than a present-error check.
